subject: Embeddings persistence: fallthrough connector, SLAs, and commercial split
messages:
From: alex@pinecone.io
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: julie@dataarc.co
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration thought — fallthrough to object store for cold embeddings

Hi Mateo,

Nice to meet you briefly at the summit last month — Alex from Pinecone (SE). We had a quick follow-up internally about customers that need a 'fallthrough' path from vector index misses into object storage (S3) for deterministic retrieval + re-embedding.

A couple quick questions we usually scope up front so we can size indexing and replication requirements:
- Expected read QPS for fallthrough path (per customer)
- TTL / retention expectations for the object-store copies
- Whether Redwood wants the connector to manage re-embedding or hand back an object URL for on-demand re-embedding

We think a joint POC could be 4 weeks (adapter + test harness) and would like to propose involving DataArc for the connector contracting. Are you available next week for a 30-min scoping call?

Cheers,
Alex Johnson
Solutions Engineer, Pinecone

P.S. attach: simple sequence diagram we sketched — happy to iterate.
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: alex@pinecone.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration thought — fallthrough to object store for cold embeddings

Alex — thanks, this is top of mind for a few mid-market customers. Quick notes from our side: 
- Read QPS: pilot customers ~50 rps, steady-state 200–300 rps on peak.
- TTL: default 90 days, with Tiered policy (30d hot, 90d warm, archive >90).
- Re-embedding model: Redwood prefers the connector to optionally kick off re-embedding jobs (async) but also return object URL if customer wants immediate retrieval.

Marissa/Neha: can you join the scoping call? Also tagging Priyom for cost model + SOW language.

I can do 1pm PT next Thu (10 Jun) — if that works I'll send an invite.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Partner Programs, Redwood Inference
From: julie@dataarc.co
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, alex@pinecone.io
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration thought — fallthrough to object store for cold embeddings

Thanks all — DataArc can handle the connector contracting and the initial SOW. A few contract items we usually ask to clarify early so there are no Git diffs during the POC:

- Ownership of re-embedded vectors (who retains derived artifacts)
- Support boundaries: DataArc supports connector ops; Redwood owns model orchestration; Pinecone owns index availability
- Cost split during POC: 60/20/20 (Redwood/DataArc/Pinecone) unless Redwood prefers to cover infra during pilot
- Target deliverables: adapter code repo, integration tests, perf report, and a 1hr handoff workshop

We will draft a short SOW and an initial SLA word doc and share by EOD Tue. Do you want us to include language for EU data residency in the same draft?

Julie Park
Head of Partnerships, DataArc
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: julie@dataarc.co, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, alex@pinecone.io
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration thought — fallthrough to object store for cold embeddings

Julie — thanks. Quick guardrails from finance/priv ops:
- During pilot Redwood will cover AWS S3 storage up to $2000/month per pilot; any additional infra consumption will be billed to partner unless pre-approved.
- Intellectual property: Redwood will request joint ownership of the adapter with permissive license for customers; DataArc we generally accept work-for-hire clauses but want to see scope.
- SLA asks: 99.9% index availability for production; POC will use 99.0% LOE metrics.

I agree to the deliverables list. Please include EU residency language — we will require that any EU-customer PII remain in EU buckets and that re-embedding jobs for EU data run in EU-internal infra.

— Priyom
Head, Partner Commercials (acting), Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: alex@pinecone.io, julie@dataarc.co, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration thought — fallthrough to object store for cold embeddings

Folks — quick update after reviewing DataArc's draft SOW and our infra team notes. Key technical points we need in SOW (added inline comments) before we sign off: 

1) Connector behavior: must support atomic write-through so that when a vector is created in Pinecone, the canonical object (raw text + metadata) is replicated to Redwood S3 with a consistent object id pattern.
2) Consistency model: eventual is fine but must guarantee read-after-write within 5s for the POC.
3) Backfill process: outline steps and metrics (throughput, estimated cost) — we saw a backfill estimate of ~300k objects, include delta-safety checks.
4) Observability hooks: push events to Redwood trace endpoint + per-object ingestion logs for audit.

Also attaching our redlined SLA term sheet and a short sequence diagram for the fallthrough behavior (see attachments). Can we aim to finalize SOW by EOD Friday (18 Jun)? POC onboarding window for customers is late July.

— Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: alex@pinecone.io
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, julie@dataarc.co
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration thought — fallthrough to object store for cold embeddings

Great notes, Marissa — appreciate the redlines. A couple commitments from Pinecone side:
- We'll scope replication tax for index writes and provide perf numbers for 50/200/500 rps within 48 hours.
- Pinecone will sign an MoU for the pilot agreeing to 99.0% availability during POC and work toward 99.9% in production SLA negotiations.
- We'll take Marissa's observability requirements and propose an events schema; should have a PR with a sample events payload by Thu EOD.

I'll coordinate with our contracts team and loop back once DataArc shares the SOW redlines. Looking forward — sounds like a solid joint go-to-market.

Alex
Solutions Engineer, Pinecone
